diffuseAlbedo.source: Z. Sang, L. Li, M. Wu et al., 'Color characteristics of plum-green celadon glaze from the Longquan kiln in Southern Song (1127-1276 A.D.) and Yuan Dynasties (1271-1368 A.D.)', npj Heritage Science 2025, https://www.nature.com/articles/s40494-025-01630-0 (X-Rite i4800): Southern Song mean L* 53.62, b* 6.74; Yuan L* 50.38, b* 7.09. Z. Ren, H. Wang et al., 'The mechanisms of color, opacifying, and cracks in celadon glazes from the Southern Song Guan Kiln', npj Heritage Science 2026, https://www.nature.com/articles/s40494-026-02383-0 (X-Rite Ci7800): L* 60 +/- 10, a* -8.49 to -2.25, b* 2.56 to 8.99, C* < 10
diffuseAlbedo.note: This is a hybrid of two kilns. Plum-green Longquan is likely greener (more negative a*) than the Guan middle. The record says 'grey-green', and plum-green is the deeper green Longquan type. Neither paper states an illuminant or observer, so the D65/2-deg label is approximate. The measurements include the body under the glaze.
diffuseAlbedo.derivation: L* and b* are the Southern Song Longquan means (53.62, 6.74). a* is the middle of the Guan range, (-8.49 + -2.25)/2 = -5.37, because the Longquan paper gives no numeric a* mean in its text (it says only that Southern Song a* was smaller than Yuan)

refractiveIndex.source: Sang et al. 2025, npj Heritage Science s40494-025-01630-0 (Longquan plum-green celadon): 'the similar refractive indices of quartz crystals (1.544) and the glass phase (1.500)', citing Pagliari et al., J. Eur. Ceram. Soc. 2013 (Pagliari not opened)
refractiveIndex.note: The paper uses this value to explain why the quartz barely affects transparency. It was not measured on the glaze and comes from Pagliari's ceramic work. My own oxide-additivity estimate for a typical lime-alkali Longquan glaze gives about 1.51, so 1.50 is good to about 0.01 to 0.02.

porosity.note: A glaze is glass: it has no open pores.

wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet.

grain.source: Sang et al. 2025, npj Heritage Science s40494-025-01630-0: average bubble size 6.87 um (Southern Song) and 8.92 um (Yuan); average glaze thickness 1.04 and 1.10 mm
grain.note: The record calls this field 'the bubbles held in the glaze'. It is measured on Longquan plum-green celadon and is about a seventh of the old 0.05 mm. Sparse larger bubbles are not captured by the mean.
grain.derivation: The Southern Song mean bubble size, 6.87 um, rounded to 0.007 mm

bed.note: The coarsest structure the face shows.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
